channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Australian Dollar slides as US yields jump before pivotal CPI
item.description: The Australian Dollar ended Thursday’s session with a 0.80% loss against the US Dollar after US producer inflation exceeded estimates, triggering pricing for a more hawkish Federal Reserve. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7159 after reaching a peak of 0.7223.

item.title: Gold falls below $4,350 as rising oil prices, US PPI reinforces Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to near $4,320 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal faces some selling pressure after the US Producer Price Index (PPI) inflation data and rising oil prices increased bets for a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Yen strength keeps 110.00 in sight
item.description: The Australian Dollar weakens versus the Japanese Yen as risk-appetite shifted sour due to the escalation of the US-Iran conflict, which has broadened to a fight between Yemen’s Houthis vs Saudi Arabia, who fight for control of the Red Sea. The AUD/JPY exchange rate is 110.53, down 0.27%.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar steadies after two-month low slide
item.description: NZD/USD is clinging to the 0.5800 mark at the start of the Asian session on Friday after dipping to a near two-month low around 0.5797 earlier in the American session.

item.title: WTI blasts past $100 as Red Sea, Hormuz risks collide
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude Oil benchmark, rises more than 7% as attacks in the Middle East intensify, driving WTI above the $ 100-per-barrel barrier for the first time since May 2026. At the time of writing, WTI trades at $103.86 after bouncing off lows of $95.37.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rebounds on hot PPI ahead of US CPI
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) reclaimed the 99.00 barrier and then some, rebounding firmly as the hot Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 5.4% over the year to August, hardening expectations for a Fed rate hike at next week's meeting.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Head-and-shoulders break puts $60 back in play
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price erases Wednesday's gains and forms a bearish head-and-shoulders chart pattern on Thursday after the white metal tanks and breaks a support trendline around $64.00-$64.15, exacerbating the decline below $63.50. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades at $63.72, down over 5.30%.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Uptrend eyes breakout 6.7000 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann keep a negative stance on USD/CNH around 6.7060, though recent price action has been confined to 6.7033–6.7074. They see current moves as range trading between 6.7030 and 6.7100 intraday.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi breaks below 0.5800 as bears take control
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) fails to clear a confluence of key Simple Moving Averages (SMAs) and dives below 0.5800 on Thursday, printing a near two-month low of 0.5797. At the time of writing, NZD/USD is down 0.65% and poised to test lower levels if it closes below 0.5800.

item.title: Malaysia Ringgit: BNM hawkish tilt limits downside – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank notes USD/MYR has risen to 4.07, marking a fourth consecutive session of Ringgit weakness, weighed by foreign portfolio outflows from Malaysian equities.

item.title: WTI Oil nears $100 as Middle East tensions keep supply concerns elevated
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil rallies nearly 5% on Thursday, climbing to its highest level since May 21 as escalating tensions in the Middle East raise fears of further disruption to already tight supplies. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $99 and is up about 10.50% so far this week.

item.title: ECB sources say further tightening remains likely – Reuters
item.description: According to Reuters sources, the European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to further tighten monetary policy in the months ahead and could raise rates in October.

item.title: Gold bulls blink as hot US PPI, $100 Oil send yields flying
item.description: Gold price retraces by about 0.90% on Thursday as traders price in a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) following the release of the US Producer Price Index (PPI) for August.

item.title: Euro steadies against the Yen after ECB lifts rates
item.description: EUR/JPY rises above the 179.00 mark on Thursday in the aftermath of the European Central Bank (ECB) raising its deposit rate by a quarter point to 2.50%, its second hike since the US-Iran war broke out.

item.title: ECB recap: A hawkish hike despite downside growth risks
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) increased the Deposit Facility Rate to 2.50%, the Refinancing Rate to 2.65% and the Marginal Lending Facility to 2.90%, effective from September 16.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Defensive Yen as BoJ turns hawkish – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight that USD/JPY is edging higher as the Japanese Yen trades defensively after its sharp late-August rally. The Bank of Japan’s messaging is described as unequivocally hawkish ahead of a widely anticipated 25 bps hike on September 18.

item.title: Canadian Dollar firms as US Dollar loses momentum, Oil prices extend rally
item.description: USD/CAD pares earlier gains on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) loses momentum after staging a modest recovery, despite US Producer Price Index (PPI) data showing that producer inflation picked up again in August. At the same time, higher Oil prices offer support to the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: Copper: Tariff uncertainty and max CTA length – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities analysts Ryan McKay and Bart Melek report that Copper’s recent rally has been driven mainly by supply-side factors linked to tariff-induced inventory depletion.

item.title: Silver slides below $65 as US PPI reinforces Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its sharp decline on Thursday, trading around $64.35 per ounce at the time of writing, down 4.39% on the day.

item.title: British Pound under pressure as hot PPI puts Fed hike in play
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) loses traction against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after the latest US producer inflation report, which exceeded estimates, prompting investors to price in a more hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed). At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades at 1.3525, down 0.17%.

item.title: British Pound: Consolidation against US Dollar before UK data and BoE – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note GBP/USD is little changed as it extends its recovery from last week’s lows, with risk set to rise on upcoming United Kingdom (UK) trade and industrial data.

item.title: United States: Higher August forecast with methodology shift – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz raise their August core PCE forecast after stronger PCE-relevant components in the August PPI report. They now expect core PCE at 0.24% m/m and 3.3% y/y, with headline PCE at 0.33% m/m and 3.8% y/y.

item.title: Australian Dollar eases from four-month high
item.description: The Australian Dollar eased against the US Dollar on Thursday, slipping back below the 0.7200 mark after touching its highest level since mid-May earlier in the week. AUD/USD trades in the 0.7160 area, lower on the day, as a firmer US Dollar pulls the pair away from a recent peak around 0.7220.

item.title: Gold slides as US PPI reinforces Fed hike expectations, US Dollar and yields rise
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades with a downside bias on Thursday as a steady US Dollar (USD), rising US Treasury yields and Federal Reserve (Fed) rate-hike expectations weigh on the precious metal, while traders also assess the latest US Producer Price Index (PPI) data.

item.title: European Central Bank: Two more hikes remain the baseline – Nordea
item.description: Nordea analysts Jan von Gerich and Tuuli Koivu note that the European Central Bank (ECB) delivered a 25bp rate hike and signalled a bias toward further tightening as its projections show Eurozone inflation above target through 2028.

item.title: Euro gains modestly against British Pound after ECB delivers widely expected hike
item.description: EUR/GBP trades with a modest positive bias on Thursday but stays within the narrow range that has been in place for more than a week.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Range trade with upside bias against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note USD/CAD is holding a tight sideways range near 1.38 with no domestic data, leaving the Canadian Dollar (CAD) driven by external factors and technicals.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ risks skewed to stronger Yen – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman's (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the recent USD/JPY decline has stalled despite hawkish comments from Bank of Japan (BoJ) member Kazuyuki Masu, with markets already pricing a 25 bps hike to 1.25% on September 18.

item.title: Japanese Yen comes under pressure as US PPI data boost US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY advances to around 154.15 on Thursday at the time of writing, up 0.40% on the day. The pair benefits from a rebound in the US Dollar (USD), supported by US data showing accelerating producer price pressures and a still-resilient labor market.

item.title: Copper: Record prices with real constraints – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Kyle Dahms highlights that Copper has reached a fresh nominal record, driven by AI-related data-centre demand, electricity grid expansion, tariff-driven stockpiling and supply disruptions.
